messages:
alex: Quick PR up for the Dedicated capacity handbook — I did a round of link cleanup (anchors, dead links) and added a new examples dir with migration payloads and a tiny mock server example. asking for a quick pass on wording, and whether the example payloads are realistic for tenant migrations.
sarah: saw it, thanks. can you add a Python + Go SDK request/response example? people copy those directly.

alex: yup — added a python snippet and a go snippet under /examples/sdk-examples.md. also included a raw payload file: `/examples/payloads/dedicated-migrate.json` (see below).

mike: quick heads-up: SLA section still mixes "eviction" and "preemption" language. we should standardize to "preemption" for cloud GPUs and call out eviction only for on-prem reserved pools. otherwise legal will flag it.

jess: also the isolation table (handbook > tenant isolation) doesn't mention cross-region failover; we had a post-mortem about warm-standby behavior. can we add a bullet about failover ordering?

tim: I can drop a one-liner and link to the failover runbook. I'll submit a tiny PR against your branch with that line and the runbook link.

alex: thanks — expecting small commits. mike — good catch on wording. I'll change eviction -> preemption except where we explicitly mean host-level eviction (on-prem). want a short footnote linking to the SLA matrix table.

sarah: for the SDK examples, make sure the python shows both sync and async call patterns, and include token/capacity headers so users see the real response shape.

alex: added this payload (copied into the PR as a code block):

```
{
  "tenant_id": "tenant_42",
  "requested_capacity": {
    "gpus": 4,
    "gpu_type": "a100-80gb",
    "region": "us-west-2"
  },
  "workload_profile": "low-latency-chat",
  "keep_warm": true,
  "rollout_plan": {
    "type": "canary",
    "steps": ["10%","50%","100%"],
    "monitor": "p99_latency"
  }
}
```

alex: and a tiny mock server stub (node) to return the shape:

```
// express mock
app.post('/v1/dedicated/provision', (req, res) => {
  res.json({
    request_id: 'req_abc123',
    status: 'queued',
    estimated_ready_at: '2024-09-02T12:34:00Z'
  })
})
```

mike: perfect — that mock will help product teams smoke-test the onboarding flow. for the SLA wording, propose: "Preemption: best-effort notifications and relocation assistance for cloud-hosted capacity; eviction applies only to on-prem host reclaims." short and to the point.

alex: I like that. i'll patch the doc with that sentence + link to sla matrix.

jess: one more thing — the isolation examples should include a tiny decision table: "use reserved pools for regulated tenants; dedicated with VPC for internal teams; hosted for self-serve." helps less technical readers.

sarah: yes, and add the quick CLI commands for terraform snippet consumers — folks paste those into console.

alex: added a small decision table and a terraform example (CLI + sample HCL snippet). left two TODOs: (1) confirm the precise label name used in tenant onboarding (is it `tenant_zone` or `tenant_region`?), and (2) verify the preemption footnote crosslink.

docs-bot: PR opened: github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/724 — title: "handbook: capacity handbook link surgery + examples" — checks: spellcheck ✅, linkcheck ⚠️ (2 unresolved anchors)

tim: i'll take the linkcheck anchors. looks like `#tenant-isolation` vs `#isolation` mismatch.

alex: ok i'm going to merge once tim fixes anchors and mike signs off on SLA phrasing. anybody object to merging small fixes after?

mike: lgtm after wording tweak.

sarah: lgtm for examples. can you also drop a tiny changelog line so the release notes pick up the examples?

alex: done. merging after anchors. thanks everyone :thumbsup:

tim: pushed anchor fix. linkcheck passes locally for me.

alex: merged and closed PR. follow-up issues created for: UX sample walkthrough, additional SDK language examples, and a separate PR to expand the isolation runbook.

jess: nice tidy-up.

alex: thanks all — will ping product to highlight the example payloads in the onboarding checklist.
